plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SMH to 5% due to its downtrend and QQQI to 25% to favor income.
Trim SPY to 20% to cure the concentration breach and reduce overall broad index exposure.

conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a target of ~1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly de-risks the portfolio by eliminating leveraged ETFs and reducing concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest returns.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to cure the concentration breach and align with balanced risk.

balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while blending broad index and quality tech. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a focus on sustainable growth.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to cure the concentration breach, freeing up capital for higher conviction plays.
Add SOXL to 6% and SPAL to 6% to increase leveraged ETF exposure within limits.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month, aiming for stretch growth. It leans into leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware that this approach significantly raises both upside potential and drawdown risk, with leveraged ETFs subject to daily decay and rebalancing. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month, prioritizing steady monthly distributions. It significantly reduces leverage and high-beta names, focusing on income-generating ETFs and broad index. While aiming for reliable income, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
